p: Leeds has grown into one of the north's great party cities, with a buzzing centre that's packed with bars, restaurants and venues. On a Saturday night, the streets around Call Lane, the Corn Exchange and the arcades are thronged with groups out for a good time. A games bar is a handy way to keep your crew together and give the evening a bit of shape.

The city is very easy to get to. Leeds station is right in the centre, with fast trains from London, Manchester, York and beyond, and the bus station is close to Kirkgate Market. If you're coming from around Yorkshire, the train is usually the simplest way to go, as it avoids the hassle of city-centre parking.

For groups, especially larger ones, booking ahead is the way to go. Decide on your games, sort out teams and make sure everyone knows what time to arrive. Building in time for food is a good idea, so you're not running on empty halfway through the evening. Games bars work brilliantly as a first stop before heading out to the rest of the city's nightlife.

If you have time during the day, the Leeds Art Gallery and the Henry Moore Institute sit side by side near the town hall, and both are free to visit. A short trip out of the centre takes you to Kirkstall Abbey, one of the best-preserved Cistercian monasteries in the country, or to Roundhay Park, with its lakes and wide open spaces. Harewood House, a grand stately home, is a short drive north.
